objective: Before any compute is spent applying this lab's converged curved-step correction field to a second geometry, measure whether the second geometry's flow states even lie inside the region of feature space the correction was fitted over, because a correction applied outside its training support is extrapolation and the resulting run measures nothing about the correction
rationale: The single question the data-driven closure literature says decides whether these methods are useful is generalisation: a correction fitted on one geometry either transfers or it does not. This lab has now produced converged correction fields on the curved step at real cost, with two arms measured at 336 and 425 core minutes and a third at 267, and it has hill and hump families sitting beside them. Nobody has asked whether a transfer is even meaningful before pricing one. It is a standard and expensive mistake: the cross-case run is bought, the correction hurts, and the write-up says the method does not generalise when what actually happened is that every target point was outside the training support and the network or the field was extrapolating. Those two conclusions are different and only one of them is about closure modelling. THE FIRST STAGE IS ZERO COMPUTE AND CAN KILL THE SECOND, which is the pattern that has already saved this lab more than 340 core minutes: both the source correction field and the target baseline fields are on disk, the source at 21,000 cells with its matched gradient archived beside it. THE NULL, AND IT IS NOT FITTED, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MAKES THE ITEM WORK: the obvious null, that the target points lie inside the source support, has no calibration and would be judged by eye. The null used instead is a WITHIN-CASE HELD-OUT CONTROL. Split the source case's own cells into two halves by a geometric rule fixed in advance, compute the same containment statistic of one half against the other, and use THAT as the reference value. Any containment statistic must score near its ceiling on a case against itself; how far the target falls below that within-case value is the quantity, and it is calibrated by a measurement rather than by a threshold somebody chose. THE IDENTITY TEST, owner rule W dash 2. The statistic is the fraction of target points falling inside the source points' region in the invariant space the correction is indexed by. Could that be derived by construction from its own inputs? No: the two point clouds come from separate solves on separate geometries and nothing computes one from the other. But there is a real hazard of the adjacent kind and it is declared: if the invariants for both clouds are computed by the same code, then a bug in that code moves both clouds together and the comparison would be checking transcription fidelity rather than physics, which is exactly the shipped-helper blindness this lab has a defect class for. THE EXTERNAL REFERENT, named as that class requires: the invariant set and the containment idea are not this lab's and the implementation is checked against the published worked definition, with the within-case control standing as the executable check that the implementation can distinguish anything at all.
gate: STAGE 1, ZERO COMPUTE, AND IT IS ALLOWED TO KILL STAGE 2. Fix the invariant set and the containment statistic and the geometric split rule in writing BEFORE opening any field. Compute the within-case held-out control on the source case. Then compute the same statistic for each target family against the source. Three-valued. TRANSPLANTABLE if a target's containment sits within a declared fraction of the within-case control value, in which case a cross-case run on that target is a real test of generalisation and may be priced. OUT OF SUPPORT if it falls far below, in which case the cross-case run on that target is cancelled before it is bought, and the finding published is that the correction's support does not reach that geometry, which is a statement about the method that costs nothing and is worth having. NO VERDICT if the within-case control does not itself score near its ceiling, because that would mean the statistic cannot distinguish a case from itself and nothing downstream of it is readable. THAT LAST BRANCH IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT A FORMALITY: it is the fitted-first-step trap in its natural habitat, and the control is run and reported FIRST, before the target numbers are computed, so the outcome cannot be read backwards into the choice of statistic. STAGE 2, NOT REQUESTED AND NOT AUTHORISED HERE: a cross-case forward run on whichever target survives.
cost_basis: ZERO solver compute for the requested stage; both point clouds are archived arrays on this host. Scored in agent tool calls: forecast 50, in the middle of this lab's measured build-and-verify band of 33 to 72, because the item implements an invariant set against a published definition, implements a containment statistic, runs a control and then applies it to two target families. Actual counted from the executing agent's transcript. Stage 2 is deliberately not priced, and the anchor for what it would displace is stated instead: the three measured curved-step inversion arms cost 336, 425 and 267 core minutes, so a cross-case arm is a purchase of that order and the screen underneath it costs no core minutes at all.
expected_knowledge_gain: THE DISCRIMINATING OUTCOME. If a target family is out of support, the cross-case run on it is cancelled for zero compute and the lab publishes a bounded statement about where its correction's support reaches, which is a real result about the method rather than a failed run. If the targets are inside the support, then a cross-case run becomes a genuine generalisation test rather than an extrapolation exercise, and its eventual negative result would mean what a negative result is supposed to mean. Either way the interpretation of the expensive run is fixed BEFORE it is bought, which is the difference between an experiment and a demonstration. Belief is unmoved only in the no-verdict branch, and that branch is a finding about the statistic rather than about closure.

launch_prompt: Transplantability screen, stage 1 only. ZERO COMPUTE and no solver launch. Step 1: write down and COMMIT the invariant set, the containment statistic and the geometric split rule before opening any field array; cite that commit in the result. Step 2: run the within-case held-out control and REPORT IT FIRST, before computing any target number. If the control does not score near its ceiling, STOP and report no verdict; do not adjust the statistic to make the control pass, which would be fitting the instrument to the answer. Step 3: compute the target statistics and apply the three-valued verdict per target family. Step 4: do not run any cross-case case and do not modify any correction field. Record your own tool call count.
